description: Unlike the worded `is a <type-word>` (whose type word is grammar-checked at parse time), the prefix `is_a?` evaluates its second argument dynamically: a non-word type argument raises `ol-type` naming the expected concept "word" (`spec/commands.md:708`, `spec/error-model.md` `ol-type`). Measured, this implementation's checker reports nothing for this program, so Phase 2 begins and execution halts at the failing statement, keeping the `instruction` event asserted below. The type argument here is a literal, so the fault is statically knowable: `spec/tooling.md:197-200` says a semantic tool SHOULD report statically knowable uses of runtime C10 codes, so a checker that folded this call would report it at `semantic` and would also conform. The stage below records what this implementation does, not an inherent property of the fault. Issue #99; see issue #1156 for the superseded rationale and for the citation it replaced.
